title: Horizon Analytics pilot: security + performance scoping
summary: POC scoping focused on compliance gating (SOC 2/ISO), SSO/SAML integration, RBAC and audit logs plus throughput targets for a 200 reqs/min low-latency chatbot pilot. Agreed to run a 3-week pilot on Dedicated capacity with private control plane for auditability; next: SOC2 report, SSO metadata, pilot SOW and benchmark plan.
transcript:
[00:00] Samir Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we're at 14:00 UTC, I think. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Maya Rodriguez: Maya here, head of ML at Horizon.
[00:10] Evan Li: Evan, platform.
[00:12] Priya Kapoor: Priya, security.
[00:15] Lindsey Cho: Lindsey, SE at Redwood. Diego on the call but he had a calendar hop coming so he might drop.
[00:23] Samir Patel: Great. Goal for today is to lock down success criteria for the pilot, workload sizing for benching, and confirm the security gating — SOC 2, SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs, et cetera.
[00:35] Priya Kapoor: To be blunt, our security team won't green-light storage of customer PII without SOC 2 plus audit logs that show every admin action. We also need SAML SSO and SCIM for user lifecycle.
[00:46] Lindsey Cho: Totally makes sense. For SOC 2 we can share our current report and the control matrix. For the pilot we typically offer either Hosted API or Redwood Dedicated — Dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools and audit controls; Redwood Private gives a private control plane and on-prem options if you need air-gap.
[01:05] Evan Li: Can you clarify the difference between Dedicated and Private? We're leaning to Dedicated but may require private control plane for compliance.
[01:12] Lindsey Cho: Yes — Dedicated is reserved capacity in our infra with tenant isolation and stronger SLAs. Private has customer-managed networking and optional on-prem packages; it exposes KMS integration and the audit logs are shipped to your syslog/SIEM. There's also RBAC integration with SSO.
[01:27] Priya Kapoor: Must confirm KMS/HSM support too. Our policy says keys must be customer-controlled and we need envelope encryption.
[01:34] Samir Patel: We support external KMS providers and customer-managed keys for Private and Dedicated with the enterprise add-on. We'll supply a KMS integration guide.
[01:41] Noah Bennett: For the pilot workload, we want interactive Q&A with a 2–3k token average context, peak 200 concurrent sessions, roughly 200 requests per minute, median latency target sub 350ms for p50 and p95 under 900ms. Is that realistic?
[01:58] Lindsey Cho: That pattern is helpful. We'll propose a few model shapes and batching configs. For 2–3k tokens you should expect higher latency, the runtime will use KV cache and vector cache — uh, KV cash in the transcript sometimes.
[02:12] Lindsey Cho: Sorry, K V cache — that'll help for repeated prefixes. For the latency numbers you've quoted, on Dedicated with A100-like nodes we can likely hit p50 ~250–350ms depending on model quant and sequence length; p95 is trickier, but we can optimize with batching and prefix caching.
[02:30] Maya Rodriguez: What about cost? We have to justify prod run rates. 
[02:33] Samir Patel: We'll produce a cost estimate in the SOW. Redwood Optimize can recommend batching and quantization (int8/int4) to lower unit costs; we can run a benchmark matrix during the pilot to show tradeoffs.
[02:45] Evan Li: Benchmarks — we need reproducible artifacts: scripts, sample prompts, seed data, and the raw latency/throughput logs. Can Redwood push logs to our S3 or a shared bucket for analysis?
[02:57] Lindsey Cho: Yes, we can export perf traces and token-level metrics; with Private you can ship logs directly to your logging endpoints. For Hosted we provide the downloadable CSVs and dashboard access.
[03:06] Priya Kapoor: Audit logs — what granularity do you offer? We need admin actions, API keys created/used, model version rollouts and who triggered them.
[03:15] Lindsey Cho: Our Console emits audit events for auth changes, rollout events, model updates, and API key operations. Events include actor, timestamp, action, and request id. For Private we stream to your SIEM; for Dedicated we can enable longer retention and exports.
[03:28] Priya Kapoor: Retention policy? 12 months at least, tamper-evident.
[03:33] Diego Marquez (CSM): On retention, we have add-on retention bundles for 12/24/36 months; tamper-evidence can be implemented via signed logs and digest chaining in Private deployments.
[03:45] Maya Rodriguez: Ok. Success criteria — from our side: 1) functional parity with current model in terms of accuracy on our eval set (hit >= 95% of baseline NDCG), 2) p50 < 350ms and p95 < 900ms at 200 rpm, 3) audit logs and SOC 2 evidence provided, 4) SSO/SAML integration + SCIM successful, and 5) a runbook for failover/backoff behavior.
[04:12] Samir Patel: That's a good list. We should add a ramp plan to the SOW — start with 20 rpm synthetic load test, then 50, 100 then 200, with benchmark checkpoints.
[04:22] Evan Li: Timeline — how long to stand up Dedicated + SSO? We have a security review with procurement in 3 weeks.
[04:28] Lindsey Cho: For Dedicated we can provision reserved capacity in about 7–10 business days after the signed pilot SOW. SSO/SAML integration depends on your IdP — often 1–3 business days for metadata exchange + testing.
[04:39] Priya Kapoor: We'll need an IdP metadata snapshot and a test account schema. SCIM provisioning also needs attributes mapping.
[04:47] Samir Patel: Action: we'll send SSO metadata template and SCIM attribute map.
[04:52] Maya Rodriguez: For benchmarks, can Redwood run both throughput tests and real-time convo tests with our seed prompts?
[04:57] Lindsey Cho: Yes — we'll run synthetic load (locust-style) and seeded conversational tests to measure tail latency, memory/kv behavior, and token billing. We'll provide raw logs and a bench report.
[05:10] Noah Bennett: On the model side — are you bringing an open-source model or are we using Redwood-curated model variants? We need deterministic versions pinned.
[05:18] Lindsey Cho: We'll propose a model matrix: a base open model (e.g., Llama-family quantized variants), a lower-cost int8 variant, and a fallback smaller model for emergency degrades. You'll be able to pin versions and we support canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies.
[05:33] Maya Rodriguez: Fallback behavior must be auditable and not degrade security.
[05:38] Lindsey Cho: Correct — fallbacks are logged and we can set policies per route.
[05:42] Priya Kapoor: Anything about data residency? Some customers need EU-only processing.
[05:46] Samir Patel: We have region routing and can route EU traffic to EU regions; for Private deployments you can host entirely within your VPC in-region. We'll note data residency as a requirement in the SOW.
[05:57] Evan Li: What about penetration testing and vulnerability scans during the pilot?
[06:01] Diego Marquez (CSM): We have a pen-test attestations pack and, for Dedicated/Private, can coordinate on a timing window for your pen-test. We also share our internal vulnerability patch cadence.
[06:12] Maya Rodriguez: Ok good. Can you confirm which compliance docs you'll share before procurement: SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 certificate, and completed security questionnaire?
[06:20] Samir Patel: Yes. We'll share SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, encryption whitepaper, and a completed standard security questionnaire. We'll also include the control matrix mapping pilot controls to your requirements.
[06:32] Priya Kapoor: For the SAML bundle, please include SP-initiated and IdP-initiated configs and an async testing plan.
[06:40] Lindsey Cho: Noted.
[06:42] Maya Rodriguez: Any competitors or prior vendors to call out? We had a brief POC with a cloud provider that couldn't provide audit log retention beyond 90 days. That was a dealbreaker.
[06:53] Samir Patel: Competitors mentioned: Anthropic, OpenAI, cloud vendor endpoints. We'll include a short comparison in SOW notes.
[07:00] Evan Li: Ok what are concrete next steps and dates?
[07:04] Samir Patel: I'll summarize, but proposed: send SOW + pilot quote by EOD next Tue (2026-09-22), SOC2 and ISO docs by Wed (2026-09-23), SSO metadata template and SCIM map today, schedule kickoff for provisioning week of 2026-09-29, benchmark window weeks of 2026-10-06 and 2026-10-13.
[07:25] Maya Rodriguez: Procurement wants a signed pilot by 2026-09-28.
[07:29] Priya Kapoor: We'll run a security review 2026-09-24.
[07:33] Samir Patel: Great. Any other blockers?
[07:36] Noah Bennett: Just one — we need a sample bench script to run locally to validate load shape.
[07:40] Lindsey Cho: We'll include locust scripts and a sample prompt set.
[07:44] Samir Patel: Cool. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the SOW and the docs. Meeting adjourned.
[07:50] (end)
